title: Populationbased generalizability of deep learning models in bitewing caries diagnostics
summary: Dental caries is among the most prevalent diseases worldwide and represents a major pathology in clinical practice due to its substantial disease burden, including pain and functional impairment. Clinically, caries - particularly in its early stages and when located interproximally - is often difficult to detect. Therefore, radiographic examination using bitewing radiographs is routinely employed as an adjunct to clinical assessment, depending on the individual patient's caries risk. With the uprising of deep learning technologies, artificial intelligence has increasingly been incorporated into dental diagnostics. Deep learning models are trained on large datasets of diseased teeth to identify so called approximal carious lesions and provide additional diagnostic support to clinicians. The aim of the present research project is to investigate the extent to which the population characteristics and level of oral healthcare provision from which training datasets originate influence the positive predictive value, negative predictive value and sensitivity of deep learning models when applied to a different population. For this purpose, 1.000 bitewing radiographs from Saveetha Dental College and Hospitals, Chennai, India, and 1.000 bitewing radiographs from the Department of Operative Dentistry and Periodontology, University Medical Center Freiburg, Germany, will be acquired in .png format. These radiographs were originally obtained for routine diagnostic purposes; therefore, no additional radiation exposure or risks will be incurred by participating patients. All radiographs will be anonymized and processed exclusively in .png format. At no point will it be possible to identify individual patients. The images will not be shared with unauthorized third parties. The 2.000 radiographs will be independently assessed on secure institutional intranet servers by a dental student, a dentist with three years of clinical experience, and a dentist with ten years of experience in preventive and restorative dentistry. In collaboration with Nostic Solutions AG (Kantonsstrasse 150, CH-8807 Freienbach, Switzerland), three deep learning models will be developed. These models will be trained using either 400 radiographs from Germany, 400 radiographs from India, or a mixed dataset comprising 200 radiographs from each country. Subsequently, the German and Indian datasets will be analyzed using these models at different sensitivity thresholds on secure institutional intranet servers. The objective of the study is to evaluate the impact of training datasets derived from populations with different levels of oral healthcare provision on the cross-population generalizability of artificial intelligence-based diagnostic models. The findings are intended to support the optimization of AI-assisted caries detection and improve the applicability of such systems in regions with increased treatment needs.

interventions.name:
Germany Model (G)
Retrospective observational study arm evaluating a deep learning model for the detection of approximal carious lesions on bitewing radiographs. The model is trained exclusively on radiographic data obtained from the Department of Operative Dentistry and Periodontology, University

India Model (I)
Retrospective observational study arm evaluating a deep learning model for the detection of approximal carious lesions on bitewing radiographs. The model is trained exclusively on radiographic data obtained from the Department of Conservative Dentistry and Endodontics, Saveetha Dent

Cross-Centre Model (IG)
Retrospective observational study arm evaluating a deep learning model for the detection of approximal carious lesions on bitewing radiographs. The model is trained on a combined dataset comprising radiographic data from both the University Medical Center Freiburg, Germany,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients in the permanent dentition.
Availability of anonymized unilateral or bilateral bitewing radiographs acquired between 2013 and 2025 at either the Department of Operative Dentistry and Periodontology, University Medical Center Freiburg, Germany, or the Department of Conservative Dentistry and Endodontics, Saveetha Dental College and Hospitals, Chennai, India.
Radiographs allowing complete assessment of at least one interproximal surface in the posterior dentition.
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete image datasets.
Radiographs of insufficient quality or otherwise unsuitable for diagnostic evaluation.
Cases in which no complete assessment of at least one interproximal surface in the posterior dentition is possible.
